title: Billabong's First Boardshorts, Cut at Home and Sold on Consignment
conflicts: Where the first shorts were made: kitchen table at North Burleigh (Boardriders), kitchen table of a small rented flat (IDCH), basement of their home (Encyclopedia of Surfing), garage (recent brand marketing); story gives the first three with sources. Name meaning: 'oasis' (IDCH) vs Wiradjuri word for a creek that runs only in the rainy season (V&A); story uses the V&A. Who devised the triple stitch: Wikipedia credits Rena, Boardriders does not say; story does not assign it. Outcome figures (A$4.50 consignment price, A$5,000 first year, A$100,000 in 1977, A$7,500 loan in 1978, A$1 million in 1981) rest on the IDCH entry alone and are attributed to it.
notes: Weaker sourcing than the others: no loadable first-person interview with either founder exists online, so the story contains no thoughts or feelings and leans on the company's own history, the Gale company history and the Encyclopedia of Surfing (public excerpt only). Editor may prefer to hold it in reserve. Stance: complicates.
